verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：人还特许的愿，被许的人要按你所估的价值归给耶和华。
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘When a man makes a special votive offering[NOTE:1] based on the conversion value of a person to the Lord,[NOTE:2]
notes: Cf. the note on Lev 22:21. Some take this as an expression for fulfilling a vow, “to fulfill a vow” (e.g., HALOT 927-28 s.v. פלא piel and NASB; cf. NRSV “in fulfillment of a vow”) or, alternatively, “to make a vow” or “for making a vow” (HALOT 928 s.v. פלא piel [II פלא]). Perhaps it refers to the making a special vow, from the verb פָלָא (palaʾ, “to be wonderful; to be remarkable”), cf. Milgrom, Numbers [JPSTC], 44. B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 151 and 193, suggests that this is a special term for “setting aside a votive offering” (related to פָלָה, palah, “to set aside”). In general, the point of the expression seems to be that this sacrifice is a special gift to God that arose out of special circumstances in the life of the worshiper.

Heb “in your valuation, persons to the Lord,” but “in your valuation” is a frozen form and, therefore, the person (“your”) does not figure into the translation (see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 73). Instead of offering a person to the Lord one could redeem that person with the appropriate amount of money delineated in the following verses (see the note on Lev 5:15 above and the explanation in Hartley, 480-81).

verses.zh: 你估定的，从二十岁到六十岁的男人，要按圣所的平，估定价银五十舍客勒。
verses.en: the conversion value of the male[NOTE:1] from twenty years old up to sixty years old[NOTE:2] is 50 shekels by the standard of the sanctuary shekel.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “your conversion value shall be [for] the male.”
Heb “from a son of twenty years and until a son of sixty years.”
See the note on Lev 5:15.

verses.zh: 若是女人，你要估定三十舍客勒。
verses.en: If the person is a female, the conversion value is 30 shekels.

verses.zh: 若是从五岁到二十岁，男子你要估定二十舍客勒，女子估定十舍客勒。
verses.en: If the person is from five years old up to twenty years old, the conversion value of the male is 20 shekels, and for the female 10 shekels.

verses.zh: 若是从一月到五岁，男子你要估定五舍客勒，女子估定三舍客勒。
verses.en: If the person is one month old up to five years old, the conversion value of the male is five shekels of silver,[NOTE:1] and for the female the conversion value is three shekels of silver.
notes: Heb “five shekels silver.”

verses.zh: 若是从六十岁以上，男人你要估定十五舍客勒，女人估定十舍客勒。
verses.en: If the person is from sixty years old and older, if he is a male, the conversion value is 15 shekels, and for the female 10 shekels.

verses.zh: 他若贫穷，不能照你所估定的价，就要把他带到祭司面前，祭司要按许愿人的力量估定他的价。
verses.en: If the person making the votive offering[NOTE:1] is too poor to pay the conversion value, he must stand the person before the priest, and the priest will establish his conversion value;[NOTE:2] according to what the man who made the votive offering can afford,[NOTE:3] the priest will establish his conversion value.
notes: Heb “if he.”
Heb “and the priest shall cause him to be valued.”
Heb “on the mouth which the hand of the one who vowed reaches.”

verses.zh: 「所许的若是牲畜，就是人献给耶和华为供物的，凡这一类献给耶和华的，都要成为圣。
verses.en: “‘If what is vowed is a kind of animal from which an offering may be presented[NOTE:1] to the Lord, anything which he gives to the Lord from this kind of animal[NOTE:2] will be holy.
notes: Heb “which they may present from it an offering.” The plural active verb is sometimes best rendered in the passive (GKC 460 §144.f, g). Some medieval Hebrew mss, Smr, a ms of the Targum, and the Vulgate all have the singular verb instead (cf. similarly v. 11).

Heb “from it.” The masculine suffix “it” here is used for the feminine in the MT, but one medieval Hebrew ms, some mss of Smr, the LXX, and the Syriac have the feminine. The referent (this kind of animal) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 人不可改换，也不可更换，或是好的换坏的，或是坏的换好的。若以牲畜更换牲畜，所许的与所换的都要成为圣。
verses.en: He must not replace or exchange it, good for bad or bad for good, and if he does indeed exchange one animal for another animal, then both the original animal[NOTE:1] and its substitute will be holy.
notes: Heb “it and its substitute.” The referent (the original animal offered) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 若牲畜不洁净，是不可献给耶和华为供物的，就要把牲畜安置在祭司面前。
verses.en: If what is vowed is an unclean animal from which an offering must not be presented to the Lord, then he must stand the animal before the priest,

verses.zh: 祭司就要估定价值；牲畜是好是坏，祭司怎样估定，就要以怎样为是。
verses.en: and the priest will establish its conversion value,[NOTE:1] whether good or bad. According to the conversion value assessed by the priest, thus it will be.
notes: Heb “and the priest shall cause it to be valued.” See the note on v. 8 above.

verses.zh: 他若一定要赎回，就要在你所估定的价值以外加上五分之一。
verses.en: If, however, the person who made the vow redeems the animal,[NOTE:1] he must add one-fifth to[NOTE:2] its conversion value.
notes: Heb “And if redeeming [infinitive absolute] he redeems it [finite verb].” For the infinitive absolute used to highlight contrast rather than emphasis see GKC 343 §113.p. The referent of “he” (the person who made the vow) and “it” (the animal) have both been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “on,” meaning “on top of, in addition to” (likewise in v. 15).

verses.zh: 「人将房屋分别为圣，归给耶和华，祭司就要估定价值。房屋是好是坏，祭司怎样估定，就要以怎样为定。
verses.en: “‘If a man consecrates his house as holy to the Lord, the priest will establish its conversion value, whether good or bad. Just as the priest establishes its conversion value, thus it will stand.[NOTE:1]
notes: The expression “it shall stand” may be a technical term for “it shall be legally valid”; cf. NLT “assessment will be final.”

verses.zh: 将房屋分别为圣的人，若要赎回房屋，就必在你所估定的价值以外加上五分之一，房屋仍旧归他。
verses.en: If the one who consecrates it redeems his house, he must add to it one-fifth of its conversion value in silver, and it will belong to him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and it shall be to him.”

verses.zh: 「人若将承受为业的几分地分别为圣，归给耶和华，你要按这地撒种多少估定价值，若撒大麦一贺梅珥，要估价五十舍客勒。
verses.en: “‘If a man consecrates to the Lord some of his own landed property, the conversion value must be calculated in accordance with the amount of seed needed to sow it,[NOTE:1] a homer of barley seed being priced at 50 shekels of silver.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “a conversion value shall be to the mouth of its seed.”
Heb “seed of a homer of barley in 50 shekels of silver.”

verses.zh: 他若从禧年将地分别为圣，就要以你所估定的价为定。
verses.en: If he consecrates his field in the Jubilee year,[NOTE:1] the conversion value will stand,
notes: Heb “from the year of the jubilee.” For the meaning of “jubilee,” see the note on Lev 25:10 above.

verses.zh: 倘若他在禧年以后将地分别为圣，祭司就要按着未到禧年所剩的年数推算价值，也要从你所估的减去价值。
verses.en: but if[NOTE:1] he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, the priest will calculate the price[NOTE:2] for him according to the years that are left until the next Jubilee year, and it will be deducted from the conversion value.
notes: Heb “And if.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have adversative force here.
Heb “the silver.”

verses.zh: 将地分别为圣的人若定要把地赎回，他便要在你所估的价值以外加上五分之一，地就准定归他。
verses.en: If, however, the one who consecrated the field redeems it,[NOTE:1] he must add to it one-fifth of the conversion price,[NOTE:2] and it will belong to him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And if redeeming [infinitive absolute] he redeems [finite verb] the field, the one who consecrated it.” For the infinitive absolute used to highlight contrast rather than emphasis see GKC 343 §113.p.
Heb “the silver of the conversion value.”
Heb “and it shall rise to him.” See HALOT 1087 s.v. קום 7 for the rendering offered here, but see also the note on the end of v. 14 above (cf. J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 476, 478).

verses.zh: 他若不赎回那地，或是将地卖给别人，就再不能赎了。
verses.en: If he does not redeem the field, but sells[NOTE:1] the field to someone else, he may never redeem it.
notes: Heb “and if he sells.”

verses.zh: 但到了禧年，那地从买主手下出来的时候，就要归耶和华为圣，和永献的地一样，要归祭司为业。
verses.en: When it reverts[NOTE:1] in the Jubilee, the field will be holy to the Lord like a permanently dedicated field;[NOTE:2] it will become the priest’s property.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “When it goes out” (cf. Lev 25:25-34).

Heb “like the field of the permanent dedication.” The Hebrew word חֵרֶם (kherem) is a much discussed term. In this and the following verses it refers in a general way to the fact that something is permanently devoted to the Lord and therefore cannot be redeemed (cf. v. 20b). See J. A. Naudé, NIDOTTE 2:276-77; N. Lohfink, TDOT 5:180-99, esp. pp. 184, 188, and 198-99; and the numerous explanations in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 483-85.
Heb “to the priest it shall be his property.”

verses.zh: 他若将所买的一块地，不是承受为业的，分别为圣归给耶和华，
verses.en: “‘If he consecrates to the Lord a field he has purchased,[NOTE:1] which is not part of his own landed property,
notes: Heb “his field of purchase,” which is to be distinguished from his own ancestral “landed property” (cf. v. 16 above).

verses.zh: 祭司就要将你所估的价值给他推算到禧年。当日，他要以你所估的价银为圣，归给耶和华。
verses.en: the priest will calculate for him the amount of its conversion value until the Jubilee year, and he must pay[NOTE:1] the conversion value on that Jubilee day as something that is holy to the Lord.
notes: Heb “give” (so KJV, ASV, NASB, NLT).

verses.zh: 到了禧年，那地要归卖主，就是那承受为业的原主。
verses.en: In the Jubilee year the field will return to the one from whom he bought it, the one to whom it belongs as landed property.

verses.zh: 凡你所估定的价银都要按着圣所的平：二十季拉为一舍客勒。
verses.en: Every conversion value must be calculated by the standard of the sanctuary shekel;[NOTE:1] 20 gerahs to the shekel.
notes: See the note on Lev 5:15.

verses.zh: 「惟独牲畜中头生的，无论是牛是羊，既归耶和华，谁也不可再分别为圣，因为这是耶和华的。
verses.en: “‘Surely no man may consecrate a firstborn that already belongs to the Lord as a firstborn among the animals; whether it is an ox or a sheep, it belongs to the Lord.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to the Lord it is.”

verses.zh: 若是不洁净的牲畜生的，就要按你所估定的价值加上五分之一赎回；若不赎回，就要按你所估定的价值卖了。
verses.en: If, however,[NOTE:1] it is among the unclean animals, he may ransom it according to[NOTE:2] its conversion value and must add one-fifth to it, but if it is not redeemed, it must be sold according to its conversion value.
notes: Heb “And if.”
Heb “in” or “by.”

verses.zh: 「但一切永献的，就是人从他所有永献给耶和华的，无论是人，是牲畜，是他承受为业的地，都不可卖，也不可赎。凡永献的是归给耶和华为至圣。
verses.en: “‘Surely anything that a man permanently dedicates to the Lord[NOTE:1] from all that belongs to him, whether from people, animals, or his landed property, must be neither sold nor redeemed; anything permanently dedicated is most holy to the Lord.
notes: Heb “Surely, any permanently dedicated [thing] which a man shall permanently dedicate to the Lord.” The Hebrew term חֵרֶם (kherem) refers to things that are devoted permanently to the Lord (see the note on v. 21 above).

verses.zh: 凡从人中当灭的都不可赎，必被治死。」
verses.en: Any human being who is permanently dedicated[NOTE:1] to the Lord[NOTE:2] must not be ransomed; such a person must be put to death.
notes: Heb “permanently dedicated from among men.”
The words “to the Lord” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied for clarity.

verses.zh: 「地上所有的，无论是地上的种子是树上的果子，十分之一是耶和华的，是归给耶和华为圣的。
verses.en: “‘Any tithe[NOTE:1] of the land, from the grain of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.
notes: On the “tithe” system in Israel, see R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 2:1035-55 and esp. pp. 1041-42 on Lev 27:30-33.

verses.zh: 人若要赎这十分之一的甚么物，就要加上五分之一。
verses.en: If a man redeems[NOTE:1] part of his tithe, however, he must add one-fifth to it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And if redeeming [infinitive absolute] a man redeems [finite verb].” For the infinitive absolute used to highlight contrast rather than emphasis see GKC 343 §113.p.
Heb “its one-fifth on it.”

verses.zh: 凡牛群羊群中，一切从杖下经过的，每第十只要归给耶和华为圣。
verses.en: All the tithe of herds or flocks, everything which passes under the rod, the tenth one will be holy to the Lord.[NOTE:1]
notes: The tithed animal was the tenth one that passed under the shepherd’s rod or staff as they were being counted (see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 485, and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 200).

verses.zh: 不可问是好是坏，也不可更换；若定要更换，所更换的与本来的牲畜都要成为圣，不可赎回。」
verses.en: The owner[NOTE:1] must not examine the animals to distinguish between good and bad, and he must not exchange it. If, however, he does exchange it,[NOTE:2] both the original animal[NOTE:3] and its substitute will be holy[NOTE:4] and must not be redeemed.’”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the owner of the animal) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “And if exchanging [infinitive absolute] he exchanges it [finite verb].” For the infinitive absolute used to highlight contrast rather than emphasis see GKC 343 §113.p.
Heb “it and its substitute.” The referent (the original animal offered) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “it shall be and its substitute shall be holy.”

verses.zh: 这就是耶和华在西奈山为以色列人所吩咐摩西的命令。
verses.en: These are the commandments which the Lord commanded Moses to tell the Israelites[NOTE:1] at Mount Sinai.
notes: Most of the commentaries and English versions translate, “which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel.” The preposition אֶל (ʾel), however, does not usually mean “for.” In this book it is commonly used when the Lord commands Moses “to speak [un]to” a person or group of persons (see, e.g., Lev 1:2; 4:2, etc.). The translation “to tell” here reflects this pattern in the book of Leviticus.
